vulnerability.title: Netty HTTP decoder skips whitespace and control characters around header names instead of rejecting them, enabling HTTP request smuggling

fixed_releases.verified_content: At the 4.1.71 release commit both findNonWhitespace() call sites validate OWS unconditionally, and validateHeaderNameElement() rejects 0x1c-0x1f

vulnerability.category_l2: Header-name parsing: whitespace/control characters around the field name are skipped instead of rejected, so a downstream proxy sees a sanitized request

critical_operation.description: splitHeader() locates the start of the header name with findNonWhitespace(sb, 0, false). The third argument disables OWS validation, so any leading whitespace, including characters that are not legal optional whitespace, is silently skipped and the name is re-based past it. The same loop later passes true for the value side, but the name boundary has already been normalised. The header-name validators in DefaultHttpHeaders also accept 0x1c-0x1f, so control characters adjacent to the name can be stripped rather than rejected. Because Netty acts as an intermediary and forwards the re-serialized, sanitized header, an upstream proxy that would have rejected the invalid request never sees the illegal bytes, enabling HTTP request smuggling (CWE-444). The 4.1.71 fix makes findNonWhitespace() validate OWS at both call sites and rejects 0x1c-0x1f in header names.

entry_point.description: A remote peer sends an HTTP request or response whose header name is wrapped in illegal whitespace or control characters; Netty decodes it and may forward it as an intermediary.

trace.description: request decoding reaches splitHeader() when a header line is complete
splitHeader() skips leading non-OWS whitespace without validation
findNonWhitespace() only enforces OWS when validateOWS is true

No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No HTTP request was crafted and no proxy was exercised; the smuggling impact is established statically from the decoding and re-serialization path.
Only the 4.1 branch was inspected; other affected branches were not diffed.
The impact depends on Netty being used as an intermediary that re-serializes headers; a direct origin server may reject the malformed request itself.
open_questions: The precise set of characters that Character.isWhitespace() treats as whitespace but RFC 7230 does not was not enumerated beyond the cited control range.
Whether every Netty HTTP codec path reaches splitHeader() was not exhaustively audited.
